news.headline: Four T. rex Footprints Show How Fast It Walked
news.body: A high school teacher found four fossil footprints in North Dakota that were likely left by a grown-up T. rex. They stretch about 10 feet. The spacing shows the giant ambled along at about 5 feet per second, roughly the speed of a person walking briskly.

news.headline: Seals Have a Hearing Superpower
news.body: Seals, sea lions, and walruses can hear well both in the air and underwater. No other mammals can do that. Scientists scanned 217 ear samples from museums and found this ability began about 26.7 million years ago. A mother seal can even pick out her pup's cry on a noisy beach.

news.headline: Meet the Fruit-Loving Dinosaur
news.body: Scientists named a new dinosaur, Infernogallus jamesi, nicknamed the hell chicken. Its beak and jaw look made for chewing soft food, so it may have munched fruits like cherries and peaches. It might even have helped spread seeds.

fun_fact: Giraffes have the same number of neck bones as you do: seven! Theirs are just really, really long. 🦒

word_of_the_day.sentence: Seals have amphibious hearing, so they hear well in and out of the water.
